extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting speculative short fiction (Tor.com / Reactor)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for authors preparing original speculative short fiction or poetry submissions to Tor.com / Reactor, specifying acceptable length, genres, editorial values, and implicit quality hallmarks drawn from accepted work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length limit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be under 17,500 words. While the upper limit is 17,500, the majority of accepted pieces are around 12,000 words — aim for tightness within that range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted genres (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculative fiction broadly — SF, fantasy, horror, alternate history, related genres
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tor.com/Reactor publishes across the spectrum of speculative genres; submit works that fit within science fiction, fantasy, horror, alternate history, or closely related speculative modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be original (previously unpublished) short fiction or poetry. Do not submit reprints or translated works that have already appeared elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial value: diversity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editors explicitly value diversity in voices and perspectives. Submissions from and about underrepresented populations are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcoming underrepresented experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Welcomes submissions with characters and settings reflecting underrepresented experiences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that authentically represent underrepresented identities, cultures, and experiences are positively regarded; consider centering such perspectives when appropriate and authentic.

rubrics_metrics.name: High literary craft within genre frame
rubrics_metrics.description: High literary craft within genre frame
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted work typically demonstrates strong prose craft — sentence-level control, imagery, pacing — while remaining true to speculative genre conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fresh treatment of speculative concepts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors favor original takes on speculative ideas rather than familiar tropes or clichéd executions. Aim to present familiar elements in surprising or insightful ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong, distinctive narrative voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, idiosyncratic narrative voice that differentiates the story and sustains reader engagement is an important evaluative hallmark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resonant emotional core
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that pair speculative premises with genuine emotional stakes and resonance (character-driven emotional impact) are preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference/tendency toward novella-length, character-driven works
rubrics_metrics.description: Often: novella-length character-driven works (fueled the Hugo/Nebula novella revival)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the submission cap is 17,500 words, the editors have a history of publishing longer, character-focused pieces; consider whether your story benefits from extended character development while remaining under the limit.
